I've attached the redline the legal team started (starlit_sla_redline_v2.pdf) and our internal worksheet showing estimated spend. If you can send a short worked example and confirm the regional measurement, procurement will route for final approval.

Hi Olly —

Thanks for the clear ask and the redline. Short answers up front:
- Measurement: uptime for Dedicated capacity is regional by default (we measure the affected card/cluster in the region where your capacity is reserved: e.g., us-west-2).
- Remedy calc: we can provide an explicit worked example. See the attached worksheet (monthly-remedy-worksheet.xlsx) — Ben also included a couple of alternative banding approaches below.

Key notes:
- Maintenance carveouts: planned maintenance windows in the contract (standard monthly window of 3 hours) are excluded from uptime. Emergency maintenance will be considered but only for agreed incident thresholds.
- Burst/backfill: transitory node pressure that is corrected by autoscaling within your dedicated pool for <5 minutes per event does not trigger remedy. We can adjust the time threshold if Starlit wants a different tolerance.

Next steps: Ben (cc'd) will drop a worked numerical example and a proposed monthly credit table. If that looks good, I can circulate a short amendment to the SLA that codifies the regional measurement and the example.

Hi all — quick numeric example as promised (keeps the math simple):

Context/assumptions:
- Agreed monthly invoice for Dedicated capacity: $120,000
- SLA uptime target: 99.90% (standard template) measured regionally
- Remedy bands in our standard template (monthly availability):
  * >= 99.90%: no credit
  * 99.00% - 99.89%: 5% of monthly invoice
  * 97.00% - 98.99%: 15% of monthly invoice
  * < 97.00%: 30% of monthly invoice

Worked example:
- October observed uptime (us-west-2): 99.25% -> falls into 99.00% - 99.89% band
- Remedy = 5% * $120,000 = $6,000 credit applied to next invoice (or refunded on request per contract)

Notes & options for Starlit:
- If Starlit wants a narrower first band (e.g., only credit when below 99.50%), we can propose that as an amendment but it will affect pricing/commitment levels.
- We can add a monthly cap on credits (e.g., max 50% of month invoice) — standard template currently caps remedies at 30% to balance risk.
- Maintenance carveouts and minute-level tolerances are configurable; we'll call them out in the amendment.

I've uploaded a version of the table into the shared Drive link Neha added; the worksheet also includes a per-hour fault budget calculation if your SREs want that.

Happy to hop on a short call Monday to walk through alternatives.

Thanks,
